findings.message: `_block` finds `budget:` only when nothing but a comment follows it. The round-8 fix made a flow map under `roles:` or `routing:` a warning, but the same form on `budget:` itself still reads as no block at all. `load` returns every default with no warning, and `set_context` takes the `start is None` branch and appends a second `budget:` key. Fix: treat any column-0 `budget:` line with an inline value as malformed. Make `load` warn on it, and make `set` refuse it, as `_set_in` already does for an inline `roles:`.
findings.scenario:
config.yaml has `budget: {gate: block}`. `specclaw-budget roles --json` exits 0 with no warning and all `source: default`, and the hook runs on `warn`, so the operator's block is silently ignored. Then `specclaw-budget set .specclaw general 150000` appends `budget:
  roles:
    general:
      context: 150000`. The file now holds two `budget:` keys, and a YAML loader either rejects it or drops `gate: block`.

findings.message: `load` warns on a non-map `roles:`/`routing:` and on a bad `context` value, but it drops these other malformed entries in silence: a role entry that is not a block map (`general: 150000`, or `general: {context: 150000}`, which `_parse` keeps as a string); a role map with no `context` key (for example a typo, `contxt:`); and a routing value that is not a non-empty string (`frontend:` blank). In each case the default stands and nothing is said. Fix: append a warning for each of these, the same way the existing role checks do.
findings.scenario:
config.yaml `budget:
  roles:
    general: 150000`. `specclaw-budget roles --json` prints `"general": {"context": 200000, ... "source": "default"}` with an empty stderr and exit 0. The hook caps general agents at 200k, not the 150k the operator wrote, and never says so. The same happens with `general:
      contxt: 150000`.

findings.message: `estimate` skips a task that has neither `Files:` nor `Context:` with `continue`. It prints nothing for that task and does not affect the exit code. plan.md says to re-run estimate 'until it exits 0', so a task that was never sized reads the same as one that fits. Fix: print `<id> unsized` for such a task (or a summary line naming it), so 'not estimated' shows up instead of disappearing. Consider a distinct exit code too.
findings.scenario: tasks.md holds T1 (Files: src/a.ts, 36k) and T3 with no Files and no Context, which the planner forgot to fill. `specclaw-budget estimate .specclaw 001-x` prints only `T1 read=36000 context=36000` and exits 0. The planner reads the plan as fully sized. At build, `brief` then sends T3 out with no context line and no size check.

findings.message: Docs and code disagree. CLAUDE.md says the role is 'a known `role=` on the prompt's first line ..., else the agent type', which implies an unknown stated role falls back to the agent type. In the code, `stated()` raises on an unknown or empty `role=`, so the gate fails open with an error on every call (the test suite asserts this). Reword the doc to say an unknown stated role is an error and lets the call through, loudly.

Under `block`, `committing` blanks quoted text before it matches `ALLOWED`. So a hand-off run through a quoted path, `"$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/bin/specclaw-budget" handover ...`, becomes `'' handover ...` and is denied, although it is the one call block exists to let through. The unquoted form works. Either match a quoted path before blanking, or document that the call must be unquoted.
